# Appeal of Denial — ACL Reconstruction (CPT 29888)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
**Member:** Quinn Grant
**Member ID:** W553544386
**Denial date:** 2026-08-02
**Reference number:** POC-87E365CAED-66145
**Plan:** UnitedHealthcare (Commercial/ACA), Minnesota
**Governing policy:** Surgery of the Knee (Commercial), https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/surgery-knee.pdf (effective 2026-06-01)

Dear UnitedHealthcare Appeals Team,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888). My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## Why I believe this denial should be reversed

The denial states that my records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I want to walk through what my records actually show, alongside what the plan's own policy says about knee surgery.

The policy states:

> "Coverage Rationale Surgery of the knee is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances."

The policy also states that for medical necessity criteria, it defers to a separate document:

> "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP:"

I was not provided with the actual InterQual criteria text that sets out what counts as an "adequate trial" of conservative care before ACL reconstruction — the citations I have been given from the "Surgery of the Knee" policy address unrelated topics, such as unicondylar/patellofemoral knee replacement, articular cartilage repair products (TruFit), and xenograft case series in foot and ankle reconstruction. None of these excerpts state a conservative-care duration or treatment-type requirement for ACL reconstruction specifically. I am not able to quote plan language that I have not been given, and I want to be clear that I am not attributing any specific conservative-care threshold to the plan that has not actually been shown to me.

What I can state plainly is what my medical records document:

- **Symptom duration:** 24 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Physical therapy:** 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing, from 2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21, totaling 20 completed visits, as recorded in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-17, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** MRI on 2026-06-29 showing a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with a bone bruise pattern; menisci intact; no significant arthritis.
- **Function and exam:** Recurrent instability with pivoting, with the knee giving way twice on stairs; positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain.
- **No contraindications:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

Given this history — nearly two years of symptoms, a completed 10-week course of supervised physical therapy, six months of NSAID use, and an injection that gave only brief partial relief — I believe the record reflects a substantial trial of non-surgical treatment before my surgeon recommended reconstruction of a confirmed, complete ACL tear.

The policy also notes:

> "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested;"

I understand that documentation alone does not guarantee approval. My request is that the plan review the documentation above against the actual criteria it applied — not against unrelated provisions concerning cartilage repair products or joint replacement.

## Request for the criteria applied to my case

The denial notice states that this determination was made under "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria," and the policy documents I have been given reference InterQual® criteria as the actual medical necessity standard. Because InterQual is licensed software and not something I can look up myself, I am requesting — as is my right under ERISA and ACA appeal rules — that the plan provide me, free of charge, the specific InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, so that I can understand exactly which conservative-care requirement my records are being measured against.

## How I am submitting this appeal

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-01-29 (180 days from the date of the denial notice), and that the address printed on my denial letter governs where this should be sent. I am submitting this appeal through member.uhc.com and by the appeal address on my denial letter, and I am also available by phone at the number on my member ID card if additional information is needed.

## What I am asking for

I am asking the plan to reconsider the denial of CPT 29888, to review the conservative-care documentation described above, and to provide the specific InterQual criteria used in my determination in writing. I appreciate your time in reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

[Member signature]
Quinn Grant
Member ID: W553544386
[Date]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
